review_plan.walk_note: The document states two dates of service for one case: the header's 'Exam date: 10/06/2026' and the ledger's 'Service date logged for this case: 10/08/2026', under the same case reference and countersigned by the proceduralist. Nothing in the source settles which is right, so the date must be asked. No member date is entered at upload (upload.service_date null), so the conflict stays the document's own and is not a member-date conflict. The walk checks that the question is open after processing (expected_context and expected_clarifications are judged before any edit), then answers it once through the screen's context form with the documented-answer form {service_date: 2026-10-06}, standing in for the endoscopist's reply to the query. The header date is the answer because it is one of the two dates the document itself states, so the reply never brings in a date the source does not give, and it is the date in the report's identifying block. It is a simulated reply, not a reading: the source alone does not select it, and a run that picks either date without asking has failed this document. must_not_code and incomplete_services are judged after the edit. Tooling note: in the copy of ops/verify_browser.cjs read for format while authoring, planProblems refuses a context_edit without upload.service_date and contextEditPreconditions expect a member-date hold, so this plan needs the documented-answer support before it can run.
